subject: ventures/woocommerce-product-csv-check
professional: a WooCommerce developer or catalogue agency that migrates stores by CSV, who would first import the output of this checker's 'clean' verdict into a staging store and check the Weight/Length unit headers, variation parent links and price columns

evidence.correctness: Ran node --test '*.test.mjs' (38 pass). Recomputed independently (scratch script, expectations written from the documented WooCommerce CSV format and the GS1 mod-10 algorithm, not from the author's tests): (1) GTINs 4006381333931 valid / 4006381333932 -> 'should be 1', 036000291452 valid, 96385074 valid / 96385075 -> 'should be 4': all match GS1 check-digit arithmetic. (2) A 4-row variable-product file: sale-ends-before-starts, sale 10 above regular 9.99, duplicate variation Size=S, and 'L' not among parent values 'S, M' were reported on the right physical lines (3,3,4,5). (3) repair() on 'Simple','yes','$1,299.50' gave simple, 1, 1299.50 and listed each change. (4) Quoted multi-line cell: the second row is reported on its physical line 4. (5) Parent id:55 not in file -> info only; missing SKU parent -> error; grouped with no children and external with no URL flagged. All matched. Not verified against a real WooCommerce import (the source file header says none was available), so capped at 3.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked by running them: header names/duplicates, delimiter detection (; and tab), unterminated quote, cell counts, Type values, Parent links, variable without attributes/variations, duplicate SKU/ID, Excel damage in SKU/GTIN, GTIN check digit, flags, stock, dimensions, sale dates, prices, images, categories, external URL, HTML balance, encoding, repair(), findings CSV: all exercised and present in calc.mjs. Not covered although the importer defines them: Position, Low stock amount, Download limit/expiry, Tax class, Brands, Download N columns beyond name matching. Page index.html exists; llms.txt, sitemap, robots present.
evidence.verification: 38 tests pass in 0.16 s. Three seeded mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted (git status clean, 38 pass after): (M1) sale-price check '>=' changed to '>' -> 38 pass, SURVIVED (the sale == regular boundary the code documents is untested); (M2) GTIN weights 3/1 swapped -> 2 tests failed (caught); (M3) date-order '<' flipped to '>' -> 1 test failed (caught). One of three survived in core validation logic, and none of the tests compare against an external WooCommerce-produced file, so 2.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (441 lines), calc.test.mjs, usage.mjs, page.test.mjs. Pure functions, no DOM, a single parser that tracks physical lines through quoted newlines, and repair() restricted to single-reading edits. Defects: validate() is one ~240-line function; dead locals (canon in header loop, a no-op .replace(/^(attribute \d+ )(\w)/, '$1$2')); a second hard-coded kg/cm assumption in DIM_COLS and COLUMNS; Type 'variation' with Published -1 and other per-type rules not modelled; closestColumn threshold is ad hoc; a mismatched-length attribute list is not checked. Acceptable, not exemplary.
evidence.claims: The header comment in calc.mjs states rules are 'read from memory of WooCommerce's public product CSV importer documentation; no WooCommerce import was available', an honest limit. The page carries a no-warranty paragraph that says a clean result does not promise acceptance (index.html:130), plus usage tracking (usage.mjs, tested). Claims on the README (checks list, 'never edits name, description, SKU, barcode...') are backed by calc.mjs and tests; I confirmed repair() leaves those columns alone. One claim is weaker than stated: 'every problem with its line number' is overstated, since problems that fall outside the listed checks (see domain) pass silently.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a store owner with a semicolon-separated Excel export containing a variation with a typo'd parent, a duplicated SKU and a '$1,299.50' price. The tool detected the delimiter, named the lines, and repair() produced a comma-delimited cleaned file with a change list. That is a real, useful job. It breaks for stores whose weight/dimension units are not kg/cm: see domain.
evidence.domain: Compared against the WooCommerce product CSV import/export documentation and WC_Product_CSV_Exporter column naming. Agrees on: Type values and 'simple, downloadable, virtual' combos, Published 1/0/-1, visibility, tax status values, backorders 0/1/notify, Parent as SKU or id:NN, Attribute N name/value(s)/visible/global/default, GTIN column and 8/12/13/14 lengths, 'Parent > Child' categories. Departs: WooCommerce names the dimension columns from the store's unit settings ('Weight (lbs)', 'Length (in)'), so a US store's normal export is flagged 'Unknown column' and its data reported as would-not-import, a false alarm in the largest market; and the unit text in dimension messages assumes kg/cm. The importer also accepts any strtotime-readable date, so the date error is stricter than the importer, which is disclosed only partly.

defects.what: Weight/Length/Width/Height headers are hard-coded to (kg)/(cm). WooCommerce names them from the store's unit settings, so a lbs/in store's own export gets four false 'Unknown column ... would not import' warnings and its dimensions are never validated.
Boundary test missing: sale price equal to regular price is not covered; flipping '>=' to '>' passes all 38 tests.
Rules were written from memory with no real WooCommerce import or exporter fixture to test against (admitted in the header comment).
Dead code: unused 'canon' and no-op replace in the header loop; validate() is a single very long function.
Date check is stricter than the importer (any strtotime-parsable date works), so some accepted files get an error.

verdict: A compact, honest, well-tested browser checker whose core outputs (GTIN check digits, line numbers through quoted newlines, parent/variation logic, repair) recompute correctly against the GS1 algorithm and the documented import format. It is finished against its README and useful for the stated job. It falls short of the bar on verification (a seeded boundary mutation survived and nothing is tested against real WooCommerce-generated files) and on domain (hard-coded kg/cm headers falsely flag every non-metric store's export). The least-effort improvement is to accept Weight/Length/Width/Height columns in (lbs|oz|kg|g) and (in|yd|cm|m|mm) and add a sale==regular test.
